vocabulary.meaning_en: have/has + past participle: I have read four books
vocabulary.example: I have read four books this month.

vocabulary.meaning_en: have/has + been + verb-ing: I have been reading
vocabulary.example: I have been reading all afternoon.

vocabulary.meaning_en: what you have at the end (often a number)

vocabulary.example: In the present perfect, the past is connected to the present.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the state of lasting a long time
vocabulary.example: "I have lived here for 30 years" shows permanence.
How long have you been waiting?
I have been waiting for 20 minutes.
They've been waiting for a while.

fine_lines.title: I have read vs I have been reading
fine_lines.explanation_ar: البسيط يركز على النتيجة والعدد (How many? How much?): I have read 16 pages. المستمر يركز على النشاط نفسه (What have you been doing?): I have been reading.
fine_lines.explanation_en: The simple form focuses on the result and number (How many? How much?): I have read 16 pages. The continuous focuses on the activity (What have you been doing?): I have been reading.

examples.sentence: I have read four books this month.
I have been reading since lunch.

fine_lines.title: How long: long time vs short time
fine_lines.explanation_ar: مع how long: للمدة الطويلة والثابتة نستعمل البسيط (I have lived in Canada for 30 years). للنشاط القصير نستعمل المستمر (I have been waiting for 20 minutes).
fine_lines.explanation_en: With "how long": for a long, permanent time use the simple (I have lived in Canada for 30 years). For a short activity use the continuous (I have been waiting for 20 minutes).

examples.sentence: My father has worked here for 25 years.
We have been waiting for ten minutes.

expressions.phrase: How many books have you read?
expressions.example: How many books have you read this year?

expressions.meaning_en: Asking about an activity up to now.
expressions.example: You look tired. What have you been doing?

expressions.phrase: I have been waiting for 20 minutes.
expressions.meaning_en: A short activity from the past until now.
expressions.example: Where are you? I have been waiting for 20 minutes.

grammar.title: The present perfect connects past and present
grammar.explanation_ar: في المضارع التام يوجد حدثان مترابطان: شيء بدأ أو حدث في الماضي ومتصل بالحاضر.
grammar.explanation_en: In the present perfect, two things are connected: something started or happened in the past and is connected to the present.
examples: They have won two games in a hundred years.

grammar.title: Present perfect simple: result (how many / how much)
grammar.explanation_ar: have/has + التصريف الثالث. نستعمله عندما يهمنا الناتج، وغالبًا رقم: How many books have you read? I have read four books.
grammar.explanation_en: have/has + past participle. Use it when the result matters, often a number: How many books have you read? I have read four books.
examples: I have watched five films this week.

grammar.title: Present perfect continuous: activity
grammar.explanation_ar: have/has + been + الفعل مع ing. نستعمله عندما يهمنا النشاط نفسه وليس العدد: What have you been doing? I have been reading.
grammar.explanation_en: have/has + been + verb-ing. Use it when the activity matters, not the number: What have you been doing? I have been reading.
examples: She has been studying all morning.

grammar.title: How long: long time (simple) vs short time (continuous)
grammar.explanation_ar: مع how long: للمدد الطويلة والثابتة نستعمل البسيط، وللأنشطة القصيرة نستعمل المستمر. بعض الأفعال لا تأتي بالمستمر بهذا المعنى: نقول I have been married وليس I have been marrying.
grammar.explanation_en: With "how long": long, permanent periods take the simple; short activities take the continuous. Some verbs don't work in the continuous here: "I have been married", not "I have been marrying".
examples: I have lived in Canada for 30 years.
I have been waiting for 20 minutes.

questions.question: "What have you been doing?" "I ___."
questions.explanation_en: The question is about the activity: continuous.

questions.explanation_en: A short activity: present perfect continuous.

questions.explanation_en: The simple form focuses on the result.

questions.question: The present perfect continuous focuses on the ___.
questions.explanation_en: The continuous focuses on the activity.
